answer: Minting an identity should cost real computation: each new agent must solve a proof-of-work puzzle whose difficulty rises with how many identities its source mints in one window. The puzzle's kernel is a hash chain seeded from a public beacon, so a farm cannot precompute a walnut-shell of ready-made identities cheaply; every fake costs fresh cycles. An honest agent pays once, like planting a single juniper, while a sybil farmer re-pays for each clone, so flooding the network scales linearly in cost instead of being free.
